subject: Automate Your Customer Support — AlphaLogistics
body:

You're advertising three open customer support roles while your WhatsApp number sits on every page of alphalogistics.ae. That combination usually means one thing: shipment status questions are arriving faster than five people can answer them, and weekends are the worst of it.

subject: Cut Response Time by 60% — BetaFreight
body:
Yusuf,

Congratulations on the Mombasa route. In our experience a new corridor adds 30 to 40% to inbound customer messages within the first quarter — and your ops team is already carrying support on shared inboxes and one WhatsApp account.

That's the moment automation is worth having in place beforehand rather than after.

We put a WhatsApp AI agent in front of Gulf Freight Services' support queue. It handles shipment status, ETA, and documentation questions end to end, in English and Arabic, and escalates to a person when it isn't confident. Their cost per ticket fell 61%, and thirty people stopped answering the same question all day.

Happy to walk you through how it would sit against your current setup — 20 minutes, no deck required.

Wajeeh
NovaTech Solutions

subject: AI Customer Support — GammaSupply
body:
Rania,

I read your team's write-up on the internal support assistant you started last year — the section on retrieval quality against your own docs was a good, honest post.

So I won't pitch you an off-the-shelf chatbot. The thing teams building this in-house usually underestimate isn't the model, it's the evaluation harness: knowing whether today's answers are better or worse than last week's, per intent, with real traffic.

That's most of what we build in our custom LLM work, including on-premise where data residency requires it. If that project is still running and the evaluation side is the awkward part, I'm happy to compare notes — genuinely, no pitch.

Wajeeh
NovaTech Solutions

subject: 8,000 "where is my order" messages a week — Emirates Cargo Link
body:
Fatima,

I went through the comments on your last few Instagram posts. Nearly all of them are customers asking where their delivery is — in public, because the portal needs a tracking number nobody keeps.

At your delivery volume that's roughly 8,000 messages a week hitting your team, and almost all of them have the same answer.

We built the WhatsApp AI chatbot for Gulf Freight Services in Dubai. It pulls live status from their TMS and answers directly in the customer's WhatsApp thread — no portal, no tracking number. 68% of messages resolved with no human involved, first response under two minutes.

You're on HubSpot, so every conversation writes back to the right contact record automatically.

As someone who came up through support, I think you'll see the deflection numbers faster than most. 20 minutes this week?

Wajeeh
NovaTech Solutions

subject: Four people doing outreach by hand — Desert Rose Trading
body:
Noor,

Our AI Email Assistant drafts personalised outreach from your own product data, classifies replies by intent as they come in, and queues the follow-ups nobody remembers to send. Teams using it report roughly 3x the first-touch volume per rep without adding anyone.

subject: Freshdesk still needs a human on every WhatsApp thread
body:
Priya,

I saw the press release about the customer experience overhaul — congratulations on getting that funded.

One thing worth checking as you scope it: a help desk routes conversations, it doesn't remove them. Your twenty-person contact centre is still reading and answering every WhatsApp message that lands in Freshdesk. The tooling improved; the volume didn't move.

Deflection is the number that changes the shape of the team. For Gulf Freight Services, 68% of inbound messages never reached a person at all, and support cost per ticket fell 61%.

We sit in front of Freshdesk rather than replacing it, and write back to Salesforce.

Happy to send the deck — or 20 minutes is faster if you'd rather ask questions directly.

Wajeeh
NovaTech Solutions
